rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.6 describe a two-year (2013, 2014) split-split plot field experiment at Tarsus, Turkey, with own yield, soil water, ET and WP measurements. Q2: Table 1 and Section 3.4 report WP for surface drip vs subsurface drip; highest WP in both years was in SDI IF3 DI50 (21.9 and 24.5 kg m-3), and Table 3 shows irrigation system had a significant effect on WP in 2014 (ns in 2013); Section 3.1 states SDI plots received slightly less water than surface drip.
rows.notes: Own evidence on SDI and WP exists but is mixed: irrigation-system effect on WP was not significant in 2013 and WP differences between systems were small; the attribution of lower SDI water use to reduced soil evaporation is asserted, not measured, and deep drainage was assumed negligible rather than measured. Single site, single soil (clayey-silt), single crop. Only LSD and p-values given, no SD/SE/CI. No stated limitations of own results. Recommendations on 3-day frequency relate to yield/regime, not stated as conditions for SDI improving WP.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.6 describe a two-year field experiment with own measurements.
rows.notes: The study does not measure or report weed growth under either drip system. Fewer weed problems under SDI is mentioned only in the Introduction as a cited advantage (Lamm and Camp, 2007; Irmak et al., 2016). The study's own results concern yield, quality, ET, WP, IWP and net income.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.6, two-year split-split plot field experiment with own yield measurements from 28.8 m2 harvest areas. Q2: Section 3.3 and Table 4: surface drip gave significantly higher yield than SDI in 2013 (65.6 vs 59.8 t ha-1; 7.3% and 11% higher for 3- and 6-day intervals) but no significant difference between systems in 2014, supporting the 'mixed' direction. Q4: Section 3.2 and Figs 2-3 report measured soil water storage in the root zone under both systems; Section 3.1 reports ETa by water balance, with SDI water consumption slightly lower and linked to lower plant height; Fig 4 relates yield to ETa for each system. Q7: Conclusions state that 3-day frequency with full irrigation is recommended under both DI and SDI to obtain higher yield and that longer intervals with moderate-to-high deficit are not recommended for SDI or DI eggplant.
rows.notes: Single site, soil, crop and climate; plot scale. Statistics reported as LSD and p-values only, no SD/SE/CI. The authors note their system comparison contradicts a Tunisian study but do not state limitations of their own data. Q7 answered yes on the basis of the stated requirement of frequent full irrigation for the yield effect; a stricter reader might treat this as a regime recommendation rather than a condition for the SDI effect.

notes: Full text appears complete. Primary two-year field study of surface vs subsurface drip on eggplant in Mediterranean Turkey; no measurements of weeds, soil evaporation or deep percolation (the latter assumed negligible).
